peggingPanel.title: Pegging:

config.constraintHint: Pin which BOM alternative a customer's demand resolves to: for a customer + parent product (location * = any), force a specific child. Add one rule per pin.
config.constraintNoAlternatives: This case has no parent products with BOM alternatives
config.elaborateMethod: Use elaborate method selection (slower; ranks methods by commit/inventory/purchase score instead of preference order)
config.methodMaxCountTooltip: Waterfall cap: how many ranked methods may be tried per demand. 1 = single best; 2-4 = exhaust the best, resort to the next only if demand isn't met. Default 2.
config.checkSoundnessTooltip: Auto-validate every successful plan against the spec.md soundness rules (always deep — includes R8 leaf-to-root chain conservation). Result shown as a badge on the run; click to open the full report.
config.maxBomDepthHint: Maximum real-make recursion depth admitted at the reactive make-fallback site. A make alternative whose precomputed depth exceeds this cap is skipped without recursing — clamps cost on deep BOMs while still admitting structurally feasible fallbacks. Default 3; range 1–10.
config.weightsHint: Relative weights the elaborate scorer applies to commit time / inventory consumed / purchase amount. Backend normalizes so absolute values don't matter — only the ratio.
config.purchaseAllowed: Purchase allowed (uncheck to exclude buy methods from planning)
config.purchasableMaterials: Purchasable raw materials (leave empty to allow all)
config.purchasableSearchPlaceholder: Search by id, description, vendor — or wildcard e.g. 160-*
config.purchasableSemantics: Whitelist semantics: an EMPTY selection means ALL raw materials are purchasable — exactly the same as selecting every one. Select specific materials to restrict purchasing to only those. So "0 selected" and "all selected" are equivalent; to actually exclude a few, Select all, then Deselect the ones you don't want (e.g. filter 160-* → Deselect matching).
config.purchasableNone: No purchasable raw materials in this case
config.purchasablePickerHeading: Select which raw materials may be purchased (empty = all):
config.enableGlobalSchedulingTooltip: When on (default), the planner walks WOs in (priority desc, due-date asc, start asc) order and pushes a WO's start later if its required resources are already reserved by earlier WOs at the same location. Uncheck to revert to the legacy single-WO parallelism behavior.
config.consolidate: Consolidate shared components in two passes: pool on-hand inventory across competing demands (split by policy), then batch the resulting make/move/buy work orders that fall in the same scheduling window
config.bucketDaysTooltip: Scheduling window for Pass 2 (work-order batching): same-component make/move/buy orders that start within this many days are merged into one batch. 0 = one batch per component across the whole horizon. Inventory allocation (Pass 1) is unaffected — it always pools on-hand stock universally (bucket 0) for fairness across all demands.
config.maxIterTooltip: Max Pass-1 inventory-allocation passes (1–15). 1 (default) = a single fast pass, but a demand can be allocated more stock than it uses, orphaning the slack (fine when supply is ample). Set higher (e.g. 15) when supply-constrained to re-run the over-claim/compensate/converge loop, which reclaims orphaned allocations for tighter inventory utilization — at higher runtime.
config.resetDefaultsTitle: Reset planning config: method by preference (depth 1, max BOM depth 3), purchase disallowed, consolidation on (30-day bucket, fair split)

policyExp.proportionalHeadline: Proportional to each demand's requested quantity
policyExp.proportionalDetail: Each demand's share = produced × (its requested qty ÷ total requested qty). When supply meets total need, every demand gets exactly its full requirement; under shortage, every demand is reduced by the same percentage.
policyExp.priorityFirstHeadline: Priority first — lowest priority number wins, full or nothing
policyExp.priorityFirstDetail: Demands are sorted by priority (lower number = higher priority, ties broken by demand id). Each demand is fully satisfied in turn until supply runs out; any demands left over receive zero. Useful when high-priority orders must never be partially shipped.
policyExp.fairHeadline: Fair — priority first when supply is sufficient, proportional under shortage
policyExp.fairDetail: When produced ≥ total requested, behaves like Priority first (each demand gets exactly its requested qty). When produced < total requested, falls back to Proportional so every demand receives a non-zero share. Prevents the priority-first failure mode where one demand grabs 100 % of scarce stock and starves the rest.
policyExp.unknownDetail: No description available for this allocation policy.

replies.empty: You can configure method selection, purchase, or shared-component consolidation. Say "show config" to see current settings.
replies.methodDepth: Set method elaborate **depth** to {depth}. The planner will score candidate methods at the top {depth} recursion level(s). Re-run plan to apply.
replies.methodMaxBomDepth: Set **max BOM depth** to {depth}. Caps the recursion depth admitted at the reactive make-fallback site; deeper makes are skipped. Re-run plan to apply.
replies.methodMaxMethods: Set **max methods** to {n}. The planner tries up to {n} ranked methods per demand; slot 1 plans the full demand, slot 2 picks up whatever's left, and so on (waterfall). Inventory carries forward across slots. Re-run plan to apply.
replies.methodElaborate: Set method selection to **elaborate (score by simulation)**. The planner simulates each method's child materials and picks the one with earliest commit, most inventory consumed, and least purchase. Slower. Re-run plan to apply.
replies.methodPreference: Set method selection to **by preference (cascade)**. The planner tries the most preferred method first; if its child materials cannot be planned, it falls back to the next preferred method. Re-run plan to apply.
replies.methodWeightCommit: Set elaborate score weights to favor **earliest delivery** (commit 1, inventory 0, purchase 0). Re-run plan to apply.
replies.methodWeightInventory: Set elaborate score weights to favor **existing inventory** (commit 0, inventory 1, purchase 0). Re-run plan to apply.
replies.methodWeightPurchase: Set elaborate score weights to favor **minimizing additional purchase** (commit 0, inventory 0, purchase 1). Re-run plan to apply.
replies.purchaseOff: Purchase (buy method) **disabled**. The planner will not use buy methods; demands will be fulfilled from inventory, make, or move only. Re-run plan to apply.
replies.purchaseOn: Purchase (buy method) **allowed**. The planner will use buy methods when available. Re-run plan to apply.
replies.consolidationOn: Enabled **shared-component consolidation** (two passes). Pass 1: demands within the same time bucket (currently {days} days) that share a stocked component draw from one shared pool of its on-hand inventory, allocated by {mode} instead of each grabbing stock independently. Pass 2: the resulting make/move/buy work orders for the same component in the same scheduling window are batched into fewer, larger orders. Re-run plan to apply.
replies.consolidationOnModeFair: fair (priority when ample, proportional under shortage)
replies.consolidationOff: Disabled consolidation. Each demand will plan its components independently. Re-run plan to apply.
replies.periodBucket: Set consolidation time bucket to **{days} day{plural}**. Re-run plan to apply.
replies.splitProportional: Set consolidation split policy to **proportional** — output is divided in proportion to each demand's requested quantity. Re-run plan to apply.
replies.splitPriority: Set consolidation split policy to **priority-first** — highest-priority demands are filled first from consolidated output. Re-run plan to apply.
replies.splitFair: Set consolidation split policy to **fair** — priority-first when supply is sufficient, proportional under shortage so no demand is starved. Re-run plan to apply.
replies.criticalityOn: Enabled **analyze criticality**. Each successful plan will be auto-saved and analyzed for component criticality.
replies.soundnessOn: Enabled **post-plan soundness check** (always deep). Each successful plan will be auto-validated; result shown as a badge on the run.
replies.reset: Reset to defaults: by preference (cascade) method selection at depth 1, max methods 2, max BOM depth 3, purchase disallowed, consolidation on (30-day bucket, fair split), criticality off, soundness check on. Re-run plan to apply.
replies.help: I handle method selection (mode, depth, max methods, max BOM depth), purchase, shared-component consolidation, and the post-plan toggles (criticality, soundness). Try: "by preference", "elaborate method", "method depth 2", "max methods 3", "max BOM depth 4", "no purchase", "allow purchase", "enable consolidation", "set 14 day bucket", "proportional split", "check soundness off", "analyze criticality", or "show config".
